note: Cross-repository test vectors for the canonical NZB identity digest (see eNode-go docs/meta-search-torrent-usenet-plan.local.md section 3.4, and usenet-crawler docs/nzb-identity.md, which is the document a port is written from). Every implementation — eNode-go, eMuleQt and the crawler daemons — must reproduce this file exactly. Each vector carries the pre-image as text and as hex, because a digest mismatch says nothing and a pre-image mismatch says everything. Exactly one of nzb and nzbHex is set per vector; nzbHex carries the documents that are not valid UTF-8. Regenerate with: go test ./nzbmeta -update

identity.label: the baseline: one file, two articles
identity.note: Read this one first. Everything below is a variation on it, and most of them must produce this exact digest.
identity.nzb:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<nzb xmlns="http://www.newzbin.com/DTD/2003/nzb">
  <file poster="p@example.invalid" date="1700000000" subject="[1/1] - "rel.part01.rar" yEnc (1/2)">
    <groups><group>alt.binaries.test</group></groups>
    <segments>
      <segment bytes="700000" number="1">a1@example.invalid</segment>
      <segment bytes="700001" number="2">a2@example.invalid</segment>
    </segments>
  </file>
</nzb>

identity.label: two files, taken in document order
identity.note: The second file's articles follow the first's, whatever their numbers are.

identity.label: segments shuffled in the XML
identity.note: Rule 2: sorted ascending by @number, so the XML order does not matter. Same digest as the baseline.
identity.nzb:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<nzb xmlns="http://www.newzbin.com/DTD/2003/nzb">
  <file poster="p@example.invalid" date="1700000000" subject="[1/1] - "rel.part01.rar" yEnc (1/2)">
    <groups><group>alt.binaries.test</group></groups>
    <segments>
      <segment bytes="700001" number="2">a2@example.invalid</segment>
      <segment bytes="700000" number="1">a1@example.invalid</segment>
    </segments>
  </file>
</nzb>

identity.label: a padded @number, an absent one and a duplicate
identity.note: Rules 2, 3 and 4: "007" is 7, an absent number is 0, and two segments claiming one number keep their document order.

identity.label: a bracketed id beside a bare one, and one carrying an entity
identity.note: Rule 5: entities resolved, whitespace trimmed, one angle bracket off each end. All three ids are written differently and read the same way.

identity.label: a zero-segment file beside a good one
identity.note: Rule 6, the load-bearing one: the empty file contributes nothing, so a reader that drops it and one that keeps it agree. This implementation drops it, and reports it as droppedFiles.

identity.label: a head with a password, which does not move the digest
identity.note: Rule 8, and the property it buys: a daemon may serve a copy with <head> stripped and the client's fold check still passes. Same digest as the baseline; the meta hashes differ only by the protected flag.
identity.nzb:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<nzb xmlns="http://www.newzbin.com/DTD/2003/nzb">
  <head>
    <meta type="name">rel</meta>
    <meta type="password">hunter2</meta>
  </head>
  <file poster="p@example.invalid" date="1700000000" subject="[1/1] - "rel.part01.rar" yEnc (1/2)">
    <groups><group>alt.binaries.test</group></groups>
    <segments>
      <segment bytes="700000" number="1">a1@example.invalid</segment>
      <segment bytes="700001" number="2">a2@example.invalid</segment>
    </segments>
  </file>
</nzb>

identity.label: a wrong namespace
identity.note: Elements are matched on their local name. Same digest as the baseline.
identity.nzb:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<nzb xmlns="http://example.invalid/not-nzb">
  <file poster="p@example.invalid" date="1700000000" subject="[1/1] - "rel.part01.rar" yEnc (1/2)">
    <groups><group>alt.binaries.test</group></groups>
    <segments>
      <segment bytes="700000" number="1">a1@example.invalid</segment>
      <segment bytes="700001" number="2">a2@example.invalid</segment>
    </segments>
  </file>
</nzb>

identity.label: no namespace at all
identity.nzb:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<nzb>
  <file poster="p@example.invalid" date="1700000000" subject="[1/1] - "rel.part01.rar" yEnc (1/2)">
    <groups><group>alt.binaries.test</group></groups>
    <segments>
      <segment bytes="700000" number="1">a1@example.invalid</segment>
      <segment bytes="700001" number="2">a2@example.invalid</segment>
    </segments>
  </file>
</nzb>

identity.label: a multi-file release, which has a whole-set row
identity.note: Three files, so wholeSetMetaHashHex is present and every row shares the ten digest bytes. A single-file release has no whole-set row at all.
identity.nzb:
<nzb xmlns="http://www.newzbin.com/DTD/2003/nzb">
  <file subject="[1/3] - "rel.part01.rar" yEnc (1/2)">
    <segments>
      <segment bytes="700000" number="1">a1@example.invalid</segment>
      <segment bytes="700000" number="2">a2@example.invalid</segment>
    </segments>
  </file>
  <file subject="[2/3] - "rel.nfo" yEnc (1/1)">
    <segments><segment bytes="2000" number="1">n1@example.invalid</segment></segments>
  </file>
  <file subject="[3/3] - "rel.vol000+01.par2" yEnc (1/1)">
    <segments><segment bytes="700000" number="1">v1@example.invalid</segment></segments>
  </file>
</nzb>

identity.label: an invalid-UTF-8 subject, repaired
identity.note: The document claims UTF-8 and carries a latin-1 byte. It is repaired rather than refused, because Qt's codec substitutes where Go's decoder errors, and the bytes the digest covers are ASCII either way — so the digest is the baseline's.

identity.label: a latin-1 declaration, transcoded
identity.note: The one non-UTF-8 charset this package reads. Nothing is flagged, because nothing was guessed.

sameIdentity.label: a repost under a different group, poster and subject
sameIdentity.note: The whole point of rule 8. Two postings of the same articles are one release, which is what stops a re-post doubling a catalogue.
sameIdentity.a:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<nzb xmlns="http://www.newzbin.com/DTD/2003/nzb">
  <file poster="p@example.invalid" date="1700000000" subject="[1/1] - "rel.part01.rar" yEnc (1/2)">
    <groups><group>alt.binaries.test</group></groups>
    <segments>
      <segment bytes="700000" number="1">a1@example.invalid</segment>
      <segment bytes="700001" number="2">a2@example.invalid</segment>
    </segments>
  </file>
</nzb>
sameIdentity.b:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<nzb xmlns="http://www.newzbin.com/DTD/2003/nzb">
  <file poster="someone.else@example.invalid" date="1800000000" subject="a completely different subject">
    <groups><group>alt.binaries.elsewhere</group><group>alt.binaries.second</group></groups>
    <segments>
      <segment bytes="7" number="2">a2@example.invalid</segment>
      <segment bytes="7" number="1">a1@example.invalid</segment>
    </segments>
  </file>
</nzb>

sameIdentity.label: the same document with its head stripped
sameIdentity.note: What catalog.serve_password_meta relies on: redacting a password leaves the release verifiable.

sameIdentity.label: the same articles grouped into one file or into two
sameIdentity.note: A pre-image line carries no file boundary. Surprising, and worth knowing before treating the digest as a file-list comparison.

reject.label: empty
reject.reason: a fetch that returned nothing is not a document

reject.label: an indexer's HTML error page served under a .nzb name
reject.reason: it parses and lists no file; calling that an empty success puts a permanently stalled item in a queue

reject.label: truncated mid-element
reject.reason: not well-formed; a partial fetch must not become a partial release

reject.label: a document whose every segment has an empty message-id
reject.reason: every file is dropped by rule 6, so nothing is left to identify

reject.label: a well-formed document with a head and no files
reject.reason: a release with no articles has no identity
